structured_output.steelman: The CEO wants myNXU's home to be a destination rather than a pass-through to Canvas: on login a student should see something worth returning for — what's due, what's next, what changed — so return visits rise. The spec does not say this; it states no outcome, metric or content, so the first finding is that the ask itself is undefined.

ambiguities.text: "Engage more" has no definition: no metric (return visits, sessions/week, time-to-Canvas, deadline-rail clicks), no baseline, no target, no measurement window.
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: An engineer cannot choose between surfacing new content, a visual refresh, notifications or a Nexa entry point — each optimises a different number — and nothing can be declared done.

ambiguities.text: No stated reason why students do not return today (what they say, what the CEO has seen, what the numbers show).
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: Without the cause, the team will build for the assumed one; if students skip the dashboard because everything they need is in Canvas, a redesign of the shell changes nothing.

ambiguities.text: "Something that makes them want to come back" names no content. Is it existing events (deadline rail already carries due dates, grades, invoices, documents, registration) rearranged, or new data such as Canvas module progress, which may not be readable from myNXU?
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: Existing events is days of work; Canvas item-level completion is an unknown integration and could be infeasible.

ambiguities.text: Design says "n/a — no UI" while the third criterion is "look modern and clean". A dashboard change is entirely UI.
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: Engineering starts without a design and rebuilds twice, or the designer is pulled mid-sprint.

ambiguities.text: Dependencies says "none", but every dashboard surface is fed by Canvas (LTI), the invoicing provider, the ID-verification vendor and the registration window feed.
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: Any new content or reordering touches those feeds; a "tweak" that needs a new field from Canvas becomes an integration.

ambiguities.text: Out of scope is "nothing in particular". Not stated whether Canvas-side coursework, notifications/email, Nexa, or mobile are in or out.
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: Scope grows silently toward whatever makes the number move; the sprint has no edge.

ambiguities.text: Size "M — a few tweaks, maybe a week" does not match the team's bands (M is a sprint for one person; a week is S) and is stated before any content is chosen.
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: The requester expects a week; the actual band is unknown until the metric and content exist.

untestable_criteria.criterion: THE SYSTEM SHALL make the dashboard more engaging for students.
untestable_criteria.rewrite: Within 4 weeks of release, the share of active students who open the myNXU dashboard on ≥3 distinct days per week rises from <baseline>% to <target>%, measured from existing login/page-view events.

untestable_criteria.criterion: WHEN a student logs in, THE SYSTEM SHALL show them something that makes them want to come back.
untestable_criteria.rewrite: WHEN a student logs in, THE SYSTEM SHALL show above the fold, without scrolling, the next assignment due (from Canvas), any open invoice or document request with its deadline, and any grade posted since the last login; each item links to its source.

untestable_criteria.criterion: THE SYSTEM SHALL look modern and clean.
untestable_criteria.rewrite: The dashboard matches the approved design (Figma frame <link>) at 360px and 1280px widths, uses the design-system tokens, and passes the existing accessibility checks with no new violations.

hidden_dependencies.name: Canvas via LTI
hidden_dependencies.why: Any "what's next" or progress content beyond assignment-due needs data myNXU may not be able to read; item-level module completion is unknown. This is the single thing that moves the band from S/M to XL.

hidden_dependencies.name: Deadline rail and its event feed
hidden_dependencies.why: The rail already shows the events that most plausibly drive return visits; the spec would extend or reorder it but does not name it, so the team cannot tell whether this is a rail change or a new surface.

hidden_dependencies.name: Nexa support assistant
hidden_dependencies.why: If "engaging" becomes a chat entry point on the dashboard, the assistant's catalogue and record access are in scope and its owner has not been consulted.

size.risk: Unsizeable until a metric and one content change are named; if the content is existing events rearranged with a design attached, it collapses to M. If it requires Canvas module progress, it stays XL.

refinement_agenda: Agree the engagement metric, its baseline and the target — and confirm the team can measure it with the events it has today.
Pick the one content change that targets that metric (existing events reordered vs new Canvas data), with the designer producing the frame in the room.
Confirm the data source for that content, then re-size and set the out-of-scope list.
structured_output.requester_message:
This can't go to the team yet: "engage more" isn't defined, so nobody can build toward it or know when it's done.

Owed from you by Thursday triage:
1. What "engage more" means as a number — e.g. students opening the dashboard on 3+ days a week — plus the baseline today and the target you'd call a win.
2. Why you think students don't come back now: what you've heard from them or seen in the data.
3. One concrete example of what you'd want a student to see on login that they can't get from Canvas.

With those three, the team can pick the content and size it at refinement; the designer and an engineer will be in the room. Without them, it stays in Inbox.

Note the current sprint is in flight. If this jumps the queue at triage, one item already in Ready moves to the following sprint — I'll name which one on Thursday once we know the size.
